  • 2 cups all-purpose flour, plus extra for dusting

  • 3/4 cup warm water (about 110°F)
  • 1 tablespoon olive oil, plus more for greasing
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1/2 cup pizza sauce
  • 1 1/2 cups shredded mozzarella cheese
  • Fresh basil leaves, for topping
  • Optional toppings: sliced pepperoni, mushrooms, bell peppers

👩‍🍳 Instructions

  1. In a large mixing bowl, combine the flour, instant yeast, sugar, and salt. Mix these dry ingredients well so the yeast and salt are evenly distributed. This step is crucial because uneven salt can kill yeast, preventing the dough from rising properly. Once mixed, add the warm water and olive oil. The water should be warm to the touch (about 110°F) to activate the yeast without killing it. Stir everything together until a shaggy dough forms, then switch to kneading by hand or with a stand mixer fitted with a dough hook. Knead for about 8-10 minutes until the dough is smooth, elastic, and slightly tacky but not sticky. Proper kneading develops gluten, which gives the crust its chewy texture and structure.
  2. Transfer the dough to a lightly oiled bowl and cover it with a damp cloth or plastic wrap. Let it rise in a warm spot for about 1 hour, or until it doubles in size. This fermentation step allows the yeast to produce gases that make the dough airy and light. Rushing this process or skipping it will result in a dense crust. The dough should look puffed up and feel soft to the touch when ready. If your kitchen is cool, placing the bowl near a warm oven or sunny window helps speed up the rise.
  3. While the dough is rising, preheat your Blackstone griddle on medium-high heat for at least 10-15 minutes. You want the surface to be very hot so the dough crisps up quickly without drying out. To test, sprinkle a few drops of water on the griddle; if they dance and evaporate immediately, it’s ready. Preheating the griddle properly is key to achieving that signature crispy crust with a smoky char. If the griddle isn’t hot enough, the dough will stick and become soggy instead of crisp.
  4. Once the dough has risen, punch it down gently to release excess gas. Turn it out onto a floured surface and divide it into 4 equal portions. Roll each portion into a ball, then use a rolling pin or your hands to stretch each ball into a thin, roughly 8-inch circle. Don’t worry about perfect edges; rustic shapes work great here. Dust the dough lightly with flour to prevent sticking. The thinner you roll the dough, the crispier the crust will be, but be careful not to tear it.
  5. Brush a thin layer of olive oil on the griddle surface to prevent sticking. Place one dough circle onto the hot griddle. Let it cook undisturbed for about 2-3 minutes until the bottom is golden and crisp. You should see bubbles forming on the surface, which indicates the heat is cooking the dough evenly. Resist the urge to flip too soon, or the crust won’t crisp properly. If the dough sticks, give it a little more time or add a touch more oil next time.
  6. Flip the dough over using a spatula, then quickly spread about 2 tablespoons of pizza sauce evenly over the cooked side. Don’t overload it or the crust will get soggy. Sprinkle a generous handful of shredded mozzarella cheese over the sauce, then add your desired toppings like pepperoni, mushrooms, or bell peppers. The cheese acts as a barrier, preventing the toppings from making the dough soggy while melting beautifully. Cooking the toppings on the griddle also adds a smoky flavor you won’t get in a regular oven.
  7. Cover the pizza loosely with a large lid or a metal bowl to trap heat and help the cheese melt evenly. Cook for another 5-7 minutes on medium heat. This indirect heat ensures the cheese melts thoroughly without burning the crust. Keep an eye so the crust doesn’t get too dark; if it’s browning too fast, lower the heat slightly. The pizza is done when the cheese is bubbly and slightly golden.
  8. Use a spatula to carefully lift the pizza off the griddle and onto a cutting board. Let it rest for a couple of minutes to cool slightly; this helps the cheese set and makes slicing easier. Sprinkle fresh basil leaves on top for a burst of color and flavor. This finishing touch brightens the rich smoky flavors and adds a fresh herbal note.
  9. Slice your pizza with a sharp pizza cutter or knife and serve immediately. The crust should be crisp and slightly charred on the bottom, with melty cheese and fresh toppings on top. Enjoy with your favorite dipping sauces or a simple salad for a complete meal. This method works great for quick weeknight dinners or casual weekend gatherings with friends and family.

  3. Remove the pre-baked crust from the oven. Spread the scrambled eggs evenly over the crust, leaving a small border around the edges. ⏰ Total Time: N/A minutes

🍽️ Servings: 4

📊 Difficulty: Easy

🥘 Ingredients

  • 3 medium cucumbers, thinly sliced
  • 1/2 cup Miracle Whip
  • 2 tablespoons white vinegar
  • 1 tablespoon sugar
  • 1/2 teaspoon salt
  • 1/4 teaspoon black pepper
  • 2 tablespoons chopped fresh dill (optional)

👩‍🍳 Instructions

  1. Start by washing and thinly slicing the cucumbers. You can use a mandoline slicer if you want really uniform thin slices, but a sharp knife works fine too. Once sliced, place the cucumbers in a colander and sprinkle with the salt. Toss gently and let them sit for about 10 minutes. This step is crucial because the salt draws out excess water from the cucumbers, preventing your salad from becoming watery and helping the flavors concentrate.
  2. While the cucumbers are draining, prepare the dressing by combining Miracle Whip, white vinegar, sugar, black pepper, and fresh dill in a bowl. Whisk everything together until smooth and well blended. The vinegar adds brightness and a bit of acidity to cut through the creaminess of the Miracle Whip, while the sugar balances that tang with a subtle sweetness.
  3. After the cucumbers have drained, pat them dry with paper towels to remove any remaining moisture. This ensures your salad stays crisp and the dressing clings nicely. If you skip this drying step, your salad might turn watery quickly.
  4. Combine the cucumbers with the dressing in a large bowl. Toss gently but thoroughly so every slice is coated with that tangy creamy goodness. Be careful not to smash the cucumbers while mixing; you want to keep the texture light and fresh.
  5. Taste the salad and adjust seasoning if needed. Sometimes I add a little more salt or a splash more vinegar depending on how tangy I want it. This step lets you personalize the flavor before chilling.
  6. Cover the bowl and refrigerate the salad for at least 30 minutes before serving. This chilling time allows the flavors to marry and the cucumbers to soak up the dressing, making every bite deliciously flavorful.
  7. Before serving, give the salad a gentle stir to redistribute any dressing that may have settled at the bottom. This ensures each bite is as good as the first.
  8. Serve the salad chilled as a refreshing side dish. It pairs wonderfully with grilled meats, sandwiches, or even as a light snack on its own during warm weather.
  9. If you want to prep ahead, you can slice and salt the cucumbers a day in advance, rinse and dry them, then store in an airtight container in the fridge. Mix with dressing just before serving to keep the best texture.
